newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia minister shelves trip to face oil strike.
newsitem.headline: Colombia minister shelves trip to face oil strike.

text.p: Colombia's Mines and Energy Minster Rodrigo Villamizar canceled a scheduled trip to Africa and the Mideast in the face of a looming strike threat by oil workers, government officials said Tuesday.
Villamizar was due to join President Ernesto Samper and other government ministers on the 10-day trip starting Wednesday.

Leaders of the 7,000-strong USO oil workers union went into meetings with Samper, Villlamizar and newly-appointed Justice Minister Almabeatriz Rengifo at 1900 local time (2400 GMT) in an 11th hour bid to avert the stoppage.
USO representatives have declined to say exactly when an all- out strike could start if no agreement is hammered out but it could be as early as Wednesday, timed to coincide with Samper's departure.

The oil workers' key demands include an end to plans by the state oil company Ecopetrol to divide its operations into separate crude and gas operations and calls for 2,000 more workers to be taken on.
Ecopetrol and the union have been bogged down in talks since early January.

"The cancellation of the Mines and Energy Minister's trip to Africa is due to last minute commitments in this country. ..of course this includes talks with the USO union," a statement from the presidential palace said.

Earlier in the day Villamizar said the government had laid contigency plans to guarantee fuel supplies. He said there was enough gasoline to last for at least 19 days and said supplies to motorists may be rationed if any strike showed signs of dragging on.
The union has promised to paralyze all Ecopetrol's production, refining, pumping and transport operations.
Foreign multinationals believe their operations could also be hit given that the pipelines through which their crude is pumped are operated by Ecopetrol workers.
"If the government maintains its radical position then we will have no alternative but to strike," USO leader Hernando Hernandez told reporters as he headed into last night's meeting.
